bib.title: Can Large Language Models Reason and Plan?
bib.venue: preprint (a version appears in Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences)

question: Can LLMs actually do principled reasoning and planning, or only approximate retrieval?
hypothesis: LLMs perform universal approximate retrieval, not reasoning; apparent planning comes from retrieval or from humans in the loop.
contributions: Perspective arguing LLMs are approximate retrievers (external System 1)
Summarises the group's planning evaluations of GPT-3/3.5/4
Advocates LLM-Modulo generate-test-critique with external sound verifiers

results.claim: GPT-4 reached 30% accuracy on Blocks World planning instances, improving modestly from GPT-3 to GPT-3.5 to GPT-4, lower in other domains
results.setup: Planning instances from IPC domains incl. Blocks World; GPT-3, GPT-3.5, GPT-4; instance counts and prompts not given here (refs 12, 13)
results.quote: with GPT4 reaching 30% empirical accuracy in the Blocks World (albeit still lower in other domains)

results.claim: GPT-4 planning performance plummeted when action and object names were obfuscated, while off-the-shelf planners were unaffected (no number given)
results.setup: Obfuscated-name test domains from refs 11, 12; no figure given

results.claim: Self-verification worsened performance in the group's plan-verification and constraint-verification studies because the LLM hallucinated false positives and false negatives (no number given)
results.setup: Refs 9, 10 (Stechly et al.; Valmeekam et al.), not re-run here
results.quote: seem to throw cold water on this optimism by showing that with “self-verification” performance actually worsens

results.claim: Fine-tuning on planning problems gave no significant improvement in the group's limited experiments (no numbers)
results.quote: our own limited experiments didn’t show any significant improvement through fine tuning

results.claim: GPT-3.5 is described as roughly a 3001-gram model
results.quote: GPT3.5 that powered the original ChatGPT is, for example, a roughly 3001-gram model of language

results.claim: LLMs are universal approximate retrievers, not principled reasoners; nothing read gives compelling reason to think they reason/plan
results.quote: nothing that I have read, verified, or done gives me any compelling reason to believe that LLMs do reasoning/planning, as normally understood

results.claim: Recommended: LLM-Modulo, LLMs generate candidates and external sound verifiers or humans certify
results.quote: The trick to avoiding ascribing autonomous reasoning capabilities to LLMs is to recognize that LLMs are generating potential answers that still need to be checked by external verifiers.

limits: Perspective piece with almost no new data; experiments are in cited works and give no counts or prompts here
Covers GPT-3 to GPT-4 era models only
Fine-tuning experiments described as limited; more data might help
practices: Use an external model-based verifier to back-prompt and certify answers (p.2)
Use LLMs as idea generators inside LLM-Modulo setups (p.3-4)
Have humans and critics refine LLM-extracted domain models, then give them to sound solvers (p.4)

terms.definition: LLMs, as n-gram models, probabilistically reconstruct completions for the prompt word by word
LLMs' idea generation with sound external verifiers in a generate-test-critique framework with guarantees
